list the runner used to run a job. For more information, see [Viewing workflow run history](/en/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/view-workflow-run-history).\n\n### Limitations for arm64 macOS runners\n\n* All actions provided by GitHub are compatible with arm64 GitHub-hosted runners. However, community actions may not be compatible with arm64 and need to be manually installed at runtime.\n* Nested-virtualization is not supported due to the limitation of Apple's Virtualization Framework.\n* Networking capabilities such as Azure private networking and assigning static IPs are not currently available for macOS larger runners.\n* The arm64 macOS runners do not have a static UUID/UDID assigned to them because Apple does not support this feature. However, Intel MacOS runners are assigned a static UDID, specifically `4203018E-580F-C1B5-9525-B745CECA79EB`. If you are building and signing on the same host you plan to test the build on, you can sign with a [development provisioning profile](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/provisioning-profiles/create-a-development-provisioning-profile/). If you do require a static UDID, you can use Intel runners and add their UDID to your Apple Developer account.\n\n### Single-CPU runners\n\nSingle-CPU GitHub-hosted runners are available in both public and private repositories. These runners—specified using the workflow label `ubuntu-slim`—offer a lower-cost option for running lightweight operations. This type of runner is optimized for automation tasks, issue operations and short-running jobs. They are not suitable for typical heavyweight CI/CD builds.\n\n`ubuntu-slim` runners execute Actions workflows in Ubuntu Linux, inside a container rather than a full VM instance. When the job begins, GitHub automatically provisions a new container for that job. All steps in the job execute in the container, allowing the steps in that job to share information using the runner's file system. When the job has finished, the container is automatically decommissioned. Each container provides hypervisor level 2 isolation.\n\n> \\[!NOTE]\n> The container for `ubuntu-slim` runners runs in unprivileged mode. This means that some operations requiring elevated privileges—such as mounting file systems, using Docker-in-Docker, or accessing low-level kernel features—are not supported.\n\nA minimal set of tools is installed on the `ubuntu-slim` runner image, appropriate for lightweight tasks. For details on what software is installed on the `ubuntu-slim` image, see the [README file](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu-slim/ubuntu-slim-Readme.md) in the `actions/runner-images` repository.\n\n#### Usage limits\n\nSingle-CPU runners follow the same concurrency model as other GitHub-hosted standard runners. See [Actions limits](/en/actions/reference/limits#job-concurrency-limits-for-github-hosted-runners). The concurrency for the runners is determined by your plan.\n\nThe job timeout for single-CPU runners is 15 minutes. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails.\n\n### Larger runners\n\nLarger runners are available for organizations and enterprises on GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud plans.\n\nLarger runners are managed virtual machines with more resources than [standard GitHub-hosted runners](/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners#supported-runners-and-hardware-resources). They offer the following advanced features:\n\n* More RAM, CPU, and disk space\n* Static IP addresses\n* Azure private networking\n* The ability to group runners\n* Autoscaling to support concurrent workflows\n* GPU-powered runners\n\nThese larger runners are hosted by GitHub and have the runner application and other tools preinstalled.\n\nFor more information, see [Using larger runners](/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/larger-runners).\n\n## Administrative privileges\n\nThe Linux and macOS virtual machines both run using passwordless `sudo`. When you need to execute commands or install tools that require more privileges than the current user, you can use `sudo` without needing to provide a password. For more information, see the [Sudo Manual](https://www.sudo.ws/man/1.8.27/sudo.man.html).\n\nWindows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled. For more information, see [How User Account Control works](https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/security/identity-protection/user-account-control/how-user-account-control-works) in the Windows documentation.\n\n## IP addresses\n\nTo get a list of IP address ranges that GitHub Actions uses for GitHub-hosted runners, you can use the GitHub REST API. For more information, see the `actions` key in the response of the `GET /meta` endpoint. For more information, see [REST API endpoints for meta data](/en/rest/meta/meta#get-github-meta-information).\n\nWindows and Ubuntu runners are hosted in Azure and subsequently have the same IP address ranges as the Azure datacenters. macOS runners are hosted in GitHub's own macOS cloud.\n\nSince there are so many IP address ranges for GitHub-hosted runners, we do not recommend that you use these as allowlists for your internal resources. Instead, we recommend you use larger runners with a static IP address range, or self-hosted runners. For more information, see [Using larger runners](/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/larger-runners) or [Self-hosted runners](/en/actions/concepts/runners/self-hosted-runners).\n\nThe list of GitHub Actions IP addresses returned by the API is updated once a week.\n\n## Communication requirements for GitHub-hosted runners\n\nA GitHub-hosted runner must establish connections to GitHub-owned endpoints to perform essential communication operations. In addition, your runner may require access to additional networks that you specify or utilize within an action.\n\nTo ensure proper communications for GitHub-hosted runners between networks within your configuration, ensure that the following communications are allowed.\n\n> \\[!NOTE]\n> Some of the domains listed are configured using `CNAME` records. Some firewalls might require you to add rules recursively for all `CNAME` records. Note that the `CNAME` records might change in the future, and that only the domains listed will remain constant.\n\n**Needed for essential operations:**\n\n```shell copy\ngithub.com\napi.github.com\n*.actions.githubusercontent.com\n```\n\n**Needed for downloading actions:**\n\n```shell copy\ncodeload.github.com\n```\n\n**Needed for uploading/downloading job summaries, logs, workflow artifacts, and caches:**\n\n```shell copy\nresults-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com\n*.blob.core.windows.net\n```\n\n**Needed for runner version updates:**\n\n```shell copy\nobjects.githubusercontent.com\nobjects-origin.githubusercontent.com\ngithub-releases.githubusercontent.com\ngithub-registry-files.githubusercontent.com\n```\n\n**Needed for retrieving OIDC tokens:**\n\n```shell copy\n*.actions.githubusercontent.com\n```\n\n**Needed for downloading or publishing packages or containers to GitHub Packages:**\n\n```shell copy\n*.pkg.github.com\npkg-containers.githubusercontent.com\nghcr.io\n```\n\n**Needed for Git Large File Storage**\n\n```shell copy\ngithub-cloud.githubusercontent.com\ngithub-cloud.s3.amazonaws.com\n```\n\n**Needed for jobs for Dependabot updates**\n\n```shell copy\ndependabot-actions.githubapp.com\n```\n\n**Needed for downloading release assets:**\n\n```shell copy\nrelease-assets.githubusercontent.com\n```\n\n**Needed for VNet:**\n\n```shell copy\napi.snapcraft.io\n*.core.windows.net\n```\n\n## File systems\n\nGitHub executes actions and shell commands in specific directories on the virtual machine. The file paths on virtual machines are not static. Use the environment variables GitHub provides to construct file paths for the `home`, `workspace`, and `workflow` directories.\n\n| Directory             | Environment variable | Description                                                                                                                                                     |\n| --------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `home`                | `HOME`               | Contains user-related data. For example, this directory could contain credentials from a login attempt.                                                         |\n| `workspace`           | `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`   | Actions and shell commands execute in this directory. An action can modify the contents of this directory, which subsequent actions can access.                 |\n| `workflow/event.json` | `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`  | The `POST` payload of the webhook event that triggered the workflow. GitHub rewrites this each time an action executes to isolate file content between actions. |\n\nFor a list of the environment variables GitHub creates for each workflow, see [Store information in variables](/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-variables).\n\n### Docker container filesystem\n\nActions that run in Docker containers have static directories under the `/github` path. However, we strongly recommend using the default environment variables to construct file paths in Docker containers.\n\nGitHub reserves the `/github` path prefix and creates three directories for actions.\n\n* `/github/home`\n* `/github/workspace` - **Note:** GitHub Actions must be run by the default Docker user (root). Ensure your Dockerfile does not set the `USER` instruction, otherwise you will not be able to access `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.\n* `/github/workflow`",

              "preview": "\"\"\"Pydantic transport models bound request sizes before domain or SQLite work begins.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator\n\n\nclass StrictModel(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Reject accidental fields so the local API contract stays explicit.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n\nclass SearchRequest(StrictModel):\n    # Symbol syntax is audited by the domain so validly submitted bad symbols persist as failures.\n    symbol: str = Field(max_length=64)\n    asset_type: Literal[\"stock\", \"etf\"]",

                "type": "file",
                "path": "/home/brajam/repos/stock_probs/src/stock_probs/schemas.py",
                "text": "\"\"\"Pydantic transport models bound request sizes before domain or SQLite work begins.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator\n\n\nclass StrictModel(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Reject accidental fields so the local API contract stays explicit.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n\nclass SearchRequest(StrictModel):\n    # Symbol syntax is audited by the domain so validly submitted bad symbols persist as failures.\n    symbol: str = Field(max_length=64)\n    asset_type: Literal[\"stock\", \"etf\"]\n\n\nclass OutcomeRequest(StrictModel):\n    observed_close: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0, le=10_000_000)\n    observed_at: datetime\n    state: Literal[\"observed\", \"unavailable\", \"provisional\", \"corrected\"]\n    note: str = Field(default=\"\", max_length=500)\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def close_required_for_observation(self) -> OutcomeRequest:\n        if self.state != \"unavailable\" and self.observed_close is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"observed_close is required unless state is unavailable\")\n        # Unavailable is an explicit missing observation, never a price-bearing correction.\n        if self.state == \"unavailable\" and self.observed_close is not None:\n            raise ValueError(\"observed_close must be omitted when state is unavailable\")\n        if self.observed_at.tzinfo is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"observed_at must include a timezone offset\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass BackupRequest(StrictModel):\n    name: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=10, max_length=73)\n\n\nclass RestoreRequest(StrictModel):\n    name: str = Field(min_length=10, max_length=73)\n    promote: bool = False",

          "type": "text",
          "text": "## Recommended plan: recover the evidence, complete the product, verify both architectures\n\nI used **five dedicated `LUNA MAX docs` agents—one for each requested file**—and reconciled their findings with the source, tooling, Git history, and GitHub.\n\nThe session export is approximately **5 MB**, containing 80 top-level messages, 110 tool calls, and 25 subagent calls. We examined the decoded historical plans, build handoffs, QA findings, repairs, and interrupted export rather than relying on its truncated preview.\n\nThis is an implementation-ready plan. Fresh builds, application tests, and release operations belong to the build phase.\n\n### What is actually established\n\n| Area | Current finding |\n|---|---|\n| Application | Substantial FastAPI, forecasting, SQLite, dashboard, backup, browser, and CI implementation exists. |\n| Historical ARM64 verification | Recorded checks include 83 deterministic tests, eight desktop/mobile browser scenarios, MCP, and live Yahoo checks. They concern the earlier working tree and do not establish acceptance of a new revision. |\n| Current host | Confirmed `x86_64`. |\n| Current remote | GitHub `main` matches local commit `2a7a3bf`. |\n| Current CI | [The existing CI run passed](https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs/actions/runs/34549899644), including deterministic and browser/MCP jobs on `ubuntu-24.04`. |\n| Remaining acceptance gaps | Cancelled independent API/UI retest, ambiguous repair records, incomplete export evidence, missing complete acceptance matrix, and no final Astra acceptance. |\n| Native ARM64 access | You currently have none. GitHub documents native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners for public repositories; the build phase will use that route and verify actual execution. |\n\n**The existing application should be completed and strengthened, with fresh evidence attached to the exact revision being accepted.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. Execution and ownership\n\nUse three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` agents per build wave. This fits your allowance of up to six while respecting the repository’s current three-agent concurrency contract.\n\n| Agent | Sole implementation ownership |\n|---|---|\n| **SOL HIGH-A — Application/API** | `api.py`, `schemas.py`, `config.py`, `cli.py`, API and configuration tests |\n| **SOL HIGH-B — Forecasting/data** | Domain, provider, service, repository, backup, migrations, fixtures, numerical/persistence/restore tests, `tests/conftest.py` |\n| **SOL HIGH-C — Interface/tooling** | `static/**`, `tools/browser/**`, scripts, Makefile, dependency manifests, CI, OpenCode configuration, resource tests |\n\nEvery assignment must name an exact milestone or repair ID, paths, dependencies, acceptance requirements, and expected handoff.\n\n**Wave sequence:**\n\n1. Declare ownership and interfaces.\n2. Run the three builders concurrently.\n3. Wait for all handoffs.\n4. Freeze the implementation under review.\n5. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA`; docs may prepare their review concurrently.\n6. `LUNA MAX docs` finalizes records against the actual QA results.\n7. Repair failures and rerun affected checks.\n8. Complete the milestone’s export, commit, push, remote, and CI gate.\n\nAgents must use isolated databases, backup directories, ports, and artifacts. Shared-file changes receive one explicit builder owner. The coordinator handles planning, integration, status, and Git.\n\n---\n\n## 2. M00 — Reconcile the contract and recovery record\n\n**Owner: LUNA MAX docs, with coordinator evidence and ID assignments.**\n\nBefore further implementation:\n\n- Preserve and reconcile the existing uncommitted documentation changes.\n- Update the supported scope to **Linux ARM64/aarch64 and Linux x86-64/amd64**.\n- Correct historical task references and repair-ID collisions, including the separate issues previously labelled `R-M04-1`.\n- Record that the late backup retest passed `make check`; preserve the earlier failure as history.\n- Record the newly verified remote and CI results against their exact commit.\n- Establish one unambiguous final-review/export order.\n- Confirm that an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer can be invoked with the required tools.\n\n### Recover requirements missing from the condensed roadmap\n\nThe earlier approved plan contains requirements that are no longer explicit acceptance rows:\n\n- Company-name lookup and instrument identity.\n- Historical cutoff reconstruction, distinct from reopening a saved forecast.\n- Walk-forward model evaluation, baseline comparison, probability scoring, and interval coverage.\n- Historical-price and distribution charts.\n- CSV and JSON exports.\n- Automatic/pre-migration backup behavior and retention limits.\n- Explicit performance targets.\n\nDocs must map these into the existing M01–M07 milestones, distinguishing accepted requirements from optional proposals. **Anything accepted remains an acceptance obligation unless you explicitly change its scope.**\n\nThen complete `EXP-M00` before advancing.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Dependency-ordered build milestones\n\n### M01 — Portable application and accurate API contract\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Verify pinned dependencies on both architectures.\n- Build a distributable package and test a clean, non-editable installation, including static assets, migrations, and fixtures.\n- Make setup commands architecture-neutral; reconcile the misleading `install-node-arm64.sh` name with its existing x64 support.\n- Establish the native ARM64/x86-64 CI matrix early enough to verify subsequent milestones.\n- Independently retest structured 404/405 errors, OpenAPI schemas, CSP-safe API documentation, validation, and startup.\n- Confirm loopback-only operation and `/api/v1`-only browser data access.\n\n**Exit:** native installation/startup and API evidence for both architectures, then `EXP-M01`.\n\n### M02 — Complete auditability and durable history\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Verify clean migration and upgrades without rewriting an already-used migration.\n- Preserve exactly one submission event for every successful, failed, and repeated forecast request.\n- Verify immutable inputs/results and append-only outcomes/corrections.\n- Complete bounded history filtering, pagination, exports, restart, and concurrency behavior.\n- Distinguish saved-result reopening from newly calculated historical reconstruction.\n- Verify history remains usable at the agreed large-history benchmark.\n\n**Exit:** independent persistence/API matrix, then `EXP-M02`.\n\n### M03 — Forecast correctness and meaningful model documentation\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Verify both horizons independently, including completed-bar exclusion and origin/target timestamps.\n- Cover holidays, early closes, special closures, missing bars, stale data, and outside-session requests.\n- Verify arbitrary supported stock/ETF selections and expose exchange, currency, timezone, and provider limitations.\n- Confirm probability definitions, threshold ordering, interval levels, units, and reproducibility.\n- Demonstrate that future or incomplete data cannot alter an earlier forecast.\n- Implement the recovered evaluation requirements with chronological separation and baseline comparisons.\n- Exercise live Yahoo through the application/API/persistence path, alongside deterministic fixtures.\n\n**Exit:** numerical, temporal, provider, provenance, and evaluation evidence; live availability recorded honestly; then `EXP-M03`.\n\n### M04 — Beautiful dashboard and complete user journeys\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Refine the existing **Signal Ledger** design.\n- Complete forecast comparison, charts, history, reconstruction, exports, and outcome presentation.\n- Expose important timestamps and repeated-failure status clearly.\n- Independently retest mobile failure focus/scroll behavior.\n- Verify every visible control and all loading, empty, success, repeated, stale, validation, and failure states.\n\n**Exit:** visual review, browser journeys, accessibility, and API-only network evidence, then `EXP-M04`.\n\n### M05 — Reliable backups and cross-architecture recovery\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Verify archive integrity, authenticity, schema compatibility, bounds, staging, promotion, and rollback.\n- Reject tampered, truncated, forged, incompatible, and unsafe-path artifacts.\n- Document and test the separate backup trust key’s creation, storage, recovery, and missing/wrong-key behavior.\n- Test **ARM64-created backups restored on x86-64, and the reverse**.\n- Demonstrate restored history through the browser.\n- Implement recovered backup automation/retention requirements with bounded resource use.\n- Verify permissions, request limits, provider timeouts, and loopback exposure.\n\n**Important:** copying the database archive alone is insufficient for the current authenticated-backup design. The recovery procedure must account for its trust key.\n\n**Exit:** independent recovery/security evidence, then `EXP-M05`.\n\n### M06 — Complete dual-architecture quality gates\n\n**Build objectives**\n\n- Run the required checks on native `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.\n- Verify Python dependencies, Node, Chromium, official headless `@playwright/mcp`, and browser regressions on both.\n- Extend MCP verification beyond initialization to real application interactions.\n- Verify clean-host installation order, including Chromium prerequisites.\n- Demonstrate that deliberately failing required checks causes CI failure.\n- Publish task-, architecture-, and commit-labelled evidence.\n- Measure process memory, latency, disk use, and idle behavior under documented resource constraints.\n\n**Exit:** both native matrices pass; required failures block CI; then `EXP-M06`.\n\n### M07 — Integrated acceptance\n\nRun the complete journey on both architectures:\n\n**Select stock/ETF → obtain both forecasts → inspect probabilities, intervals, and provenance → find successful/failed/repeated history → reopen saved results → append outcomes → export → restart → back up → restore → reopen restored history.**\n\nReconcile the final README, agent rules, plan, roadmap, limitations, and evidence records.\n\nThen proceed to independent Astra acceptance.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Visual design brief\n\nThe presentation builder should evolve Signal Ledger into a polished financial research interface:\n\n- Warm paper surfaces, deep ink typography, restrained rust accents, and consistent spacing.\n- Clear numerical hierarchy and aligned tabular figures.\n- A compact search area that keeps useful results prominent.\n- Side-by-side horizon cards on desktop, stacked naturally on mobile.\n- Readable probability and interval graphics with equivalent tables.\n- Clearly distinguished current, stale, failed, repeated, and reconstructed states.\n- Detailed provenance available without overwhelming the primary result.\n- Locally served assets and a lightweight frontend.\n\n### Visual acceptance criteria\n\n- Review screenshots at **360, 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 pixels**.\n- No clipped content, overlapping controls, or unintended page overflow.\n- Review populated results and every important state—not only the empty screen.\n- Verify contrast, keyboard focus, touch targets, zoom/reflow, and reduced motion.\n- Include actual assistive-technology evidence; axe and keyboard tests alone do not establish screen-reader acceptance.\n- Require a named visual reviewer to record findings and repairs.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Dual-architecture verification contract\n\nThe same candidate revision must pass this matrix:\n\n| Check | x86-64 | ARM64 |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Native host/runtime identity | Required | Required |\n| Package build and clean installation | Required | Required |\n| `make check` | Required | Required |\n| Loopback startup/API smoke | Required | Required |\n| Chromium installation | Required | Required |\n| `make mcp-smoke` and MCP application interaction | Required | Required |\n| Desktop/mobile browser regressions | Required | Required |\n| Backup/restore and cross-architecture recovery | Required | Required |\n| Resource measurements | Required | Required |\n\nRecord architecture, OS, tool versions, command, UTC timestamp, exact revision, result, artifact, and reviewer.\n\nGitHub’s native ARM64 runner is the planned solution to your unavailable laptop. If it cannot execute the required checks, the affected gate remains blocked. Hosted-runner measurements must also distinguish constrained-resource testing from testing the original physical laptop.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Documentation and code comments\n\nKeep the four documentation files purposeful:\n\n- **`README.md`:** installation, startup, user guide, model interpretation, platform matrix, troubleshooting, backup/trust-key recovery, and verified limitations.\n- **`AGENTS.md`:** compact ownership rules, commands, architecture requirements, and repository-specific pitfalls.\n- **`MVP-PLAN.md`:** complete requirements, API/model/data contracts, acceptance criteria, and repair records.\n- **`MVP-ROADMAP.md`:** dependencies, current status, next actions, evidence links, and release gates.\n\nComments must explain non-obvious intent: time boundaries, leakage prevention, probability assumptions, immutable writes, restore guarantees, security decisions, and resource limits. Comment-presence checks remain useful, but reviewer judgment must establish their quality. Documentation snippets must include useful explanatory comments.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Final acceptance and recoverable checkpoints\n\nThe final sequence is:\n\n**M07 QA/docs → independent `ASTRA-FINAL` → repairs and QA/Astra retests → Astra records `Accepted` → `EXP-M07` → `EXP-FINAL`.**\n\nAstra must inventory and verify every feature, API route, UI control, browser journey, and persistence effect.\n\nFor each export gate:\n\n1. Generate the full session export at `SESSION-EXPORT.md`.\n2. Verify its coverage and review it for secrets.\n3. Commit and push the intended checkpoint.\n4. Verify the remote SHA and CI results.\n5. Record post-push receipts against that exact SHA, preserving them in subsequent checkpoints without claiming a commit contains its own future CI result.\n\n**First build-phase action:** reconcile M00 and complete its export gate, then start the three-lane M01 wave with native dual-architecture verification. The roadmap remains the acceptance contract throughout.",

An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n \n-Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n \n-This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\n+This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\n \n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n \n ### API boundary\n \n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n \n ### Data source and time semantics\n \n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n+- Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\n \n ### Persistence and auditability\n \n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n+- Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\n \n ### User experience\n \n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n+- Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n-- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\n+- Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\n \n ### Deployment and resources\n \n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n-- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n \n ## Planned Architecture\n \n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n \n The API/application layers should remain separable:\n \n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n-- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\n+- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\n \n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n \n ## Forecast Contract\n \n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n \n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n \n+The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\n+\n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\n96: \n97: ## Product Goal\n98: \n99: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\n100: \n101: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\n102: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n103: \n104: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n105: \n106: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\n107: \n108: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n109: \n110: ### API boundary\n111: \n112: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n113: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n114: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n115: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n116: \n117: ### Data source and time semantics\n118: \n119: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n120: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n121: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n122: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n123: - Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\n124: \n125: ### Persistence and auditability\n126: \n127: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n128: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n129: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n130: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n131: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n132: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n133: - Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\n134: \n135: ### User experience\n136: \n137: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n138: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n139: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n140: - Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\n141: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n142: - Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\n143: \n144: ### Deployment and resources\n145: \n146: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n147: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n148: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n149: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\n150: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n151: \n152: ## Planned Architecture\n153: \n154: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n155: \n156: The API/application layers should remain separable:\n157: \n158: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n159: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n160: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n161: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n162: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\n163: \n164: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n165: \n166: ## Forecast Contract\n167: \n168: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n169: \n170: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n171: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n172: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n173: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n174: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n175: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n176: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n177: \n178: The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\n179: \n180: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\n181: \n182: ## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\n183: \n184: These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows. Any gap requires `R-ASTRA-<n>` and QA/Astra retest.\n306: - **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M07` follows accepted M07 evidence and Astra acceptance; `EXP-FINAL` is a separate final export/commit/push/remote/CI gate after all Astra repairs.\n307: \n308: ## Evidence Record Format\n309: \n310: Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\n311: \n312: - **Task ID:** the exact `M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL` identifier; do not replace it with a generic phase name.\n313: - **Status:** exactly `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\n314: - **Owner/phase:** builder lane, QA gate, docs gate, Astra review, export, or remote verification owner.\n315: - **Dependencies verified:** completed task IDs plus the evidence references that prove each dependency.\n316: - **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\n317: - **Acceptance evidence:** one row per acceptance requirement, each with an evidence ID, command/check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and named reviewer.\n318: - **Verification result:** independent check name and exact result; a test file, source inspection, generated report, or implementation claim is not a pass by itself.\n319: - **Repair history:** every failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, or connectivity loss; include repair ID, root cause, fix, and rerun result. Use `None` only when no repair was needed.\n320: - **Limitations:** provider, environment, resource, data freshness, coverage, or artifact limitations that remain.\n321: - **Export/remote record:** export task ID, stable `SESSION-EXPORT.md` revision, secret-review result, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, and CI result.\n322: - **Reviewer:** the named independent verifying agent, and for final release the independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer.\n323: \n324: Evidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\n325: \n326: ## Verification And Repair Loop\n327: \n328: 1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence and assigns the exact task ID.\n329: 2. Three non-overlapping `SOL HIGH build` lanes work concurrently, then all builders report before integration or verification begins.\n330: 3. `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` run their independent gates after the build wait; neither masks a missing result.\n331: 4. The coordinator alone integrates, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. If any check fails, the task remains pending, in progress, or blocked; create `R-M##-<n>` and repair the root cause rather than weakening the check.\n332: 5. QA reruns the failed check and affected regression set. Documentation records the new evidence, limitation, exact timestamp/commit, and any skipped or unavailable result.\n333: 6. The coordinator marks a milestone completed only when every acceptance field, independent QA/docs review, reviewer field, `EXP-M##` export, secret review, push, remote check, and CI result pass.\n334: 7. After M07, `ASTRA-FINAL` must review the complete feature/API/UI/control/journey/persistence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>` and requires repair, QA rerun, Astra retest, and explicit `Accepted` before `EXP-FINAL`.\n335: \n336: ## Final Definition Of Done\n337: \n338: The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\n339: \n340: - M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\n341: - A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\n342: - Results contain probabilities and defined magnitude intervals with source, as-of, stale/error, model/version, input, and output provenance.\n343: - Every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search is retained, history is searchable through `/api/v1`, and forecast inputs/results/outcomes are immutable or append-only as specified.\n344: - Backup artifacts and restores are verified through integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\n345: - The frontend uses FastAPI `/api/v1` for all application data and has no direct SQLite access.\n346: - The dashboard is responsive and accessible, including keyboard, screen-reader, text-equivalent, loading, empty, stale, repeated, and failure behavior.\n347: - The default deployment is secure loopback, bounded for a low-resource ARM64 laptop, and documented with its limitations.\n348: - The official headless `@playwright/mcp` supports agent QA, automated browser regressions are checked in, and Git/CI gates fail closed on required regressions.\n349: - Code comments explain non-obvious behavior, the supported local workflow is documented, and `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are reconciled with the evidence actually shipped.\n350: - `ASTRA-FINAL` is independently recorded as `Accepted` after its complete evidence matrix and every `R-ASTRA-<n>` retest.\n\n(Output capped at 50 KB. Showing lines 1-350. Use offset=351 to continue.)\n</content>",

\"msg_08c48090c002vCRiEJZhcJ9AR3\"\n823:         },\n824:         {\n825:           \"type\": \"text\",\n826:           \"text\": \"## What this application does\\n\\nThis is a small **Python command-line prototype for estimating the probability of stock-price declines**. It combines subjective estimates, historical frequencies, and a normal-distribution model, then prints results as a table.\\n\\n### The three scripts\\n\\n| File | Purpose and current state |\\n|---|---|\\n| `prob_calc.py` | Calculates example probabilities for PayPal (`PYPL`), then prompts for a custom scenario and weights. |\\n| `prob_calc_hardcoded.py` | Currently identical to `prob_calc.py`, including the interactive prompts. |\\n| `prob_calc_yf.py` | Intended to fetch Yahoo Finance data for a supplied ticker, defaulting to `SPY`. Currently contains syntax errors and cannot run as written. |\\n\\n### How the main calculator works\\n\\nThe two identical scripts blend three inputs:\\n\\n- A subjective “Burry Gut Score.”\\n- A supplied historical frequency.\\n- A modeled downside probability calculated as `norm.cdf(-threshold / sd)`.\\n\\nThe function’s default weights are **60% subjective / 20% historical / 20% modeled**, but the example run first selects weights using a mock backtest.\\n\\nThe built-in scenarios are:\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 5%.\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 10%.\\n- A one-month pullback to $50, represented by a fixed 27.5% decline.\\n\\nThese inputs are hardcoded; these scripts do not retrieve market data.\\n\\n### What the Yahoo Finance version intends to do\\n\\n`prob_calc_yf.py` is written to:\\n1. Download 10 years of daily prices.\\n2. Measure the historical frequency of daily declines exceeding 5%.\\n3. Estimate volatility from the latest 252 daily returns.\\n4. Blend historical frequency and modeled probability with **70% / 30% weights**.\\n\\nIts output calls the modeled component “Market IV Expectation,” but the calculation uses **realized historical volatility**, not options-implied volatility.\\n\\n## Important findings\\n\\n- **The backtest is explicitly a mock.** It uses five dummy returns... Saved forecasts reopen as immutable recorded results; historical-cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis.\n-- All frontend data uses FastAPI `/api/v1`; the browser never opens SQLite, issues SQL, receives a database path, or calls Yahoo Finance directly. SQLite retains successful, failed, and repeated searches, immutable inputs/results, and append-only outcomes.\n-- Searchable history, CSV and JSON export, verified backup/restore, accessible responsive UI, secure loopback deployment, bounded operation on both native architectures, official headless `@playwright/mcp`, browser regressions, and fail-closed Git/CI gates are release requirements.\n-- Non-obvious implementation behavior needs a useful intent or constraint comment. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\n \n ### Safe build-wave ownership\n \n Use exactly three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` instances in each implementation or repair wave, never more than three. The coordinator records this lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts; the lanes cover every implementation, configuration, and test path:\n \n | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\n | --- | --- | --- |\n | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, package/launch assumptions, and transport-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\n | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and domain/storage tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\n-| `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\n+| `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/local-gate tooling, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\n \n No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MVP-PLAN.md`, and `MVP-ROADMAP.md` are documentation-owned; `SESSION-EXPORT.md` is export-owned. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\n \n ## Product Goal\n \n Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\n \n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n \n Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n \n This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\n \n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n \n ### API boundary\n \n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n \n ### Data source and time semantics\n \n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n - Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\n \n ### Persistence and auditability\n \n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n - Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\n \n ### User experience\n \n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n - Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n - Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\n \n ### Deployment and resources\n \n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n-- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource Linux x86-64 and ARM64. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU. Native x86-64 measurements are native evidence; ARM64 performance is measured only on local native ARM64 hardware. Emulation can verify packaging/runtime portability and functional/build/tool behavior, but cannot prove physical ARM64 performance.\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n \n ## Planned Architecture\n \n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n \n The API/application layers should remain separable:\n \n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\n \n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n \n ## Forecast Contract\n \n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n \n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n \n The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\n \n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\n \n ## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\n \n These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows.
